column15: Single product, no information found this session; 'Bercloux' is a commune name in Charente-Maritime, France, but not confirmed as this brand's actual origin so countryCode left empty rather than guessed

Bernheim Original, a straight wheat whiskey made by Heaven Hill at their (New) Bernheim distillery, Louisville. defaultTypeName left empty since "wheat whiskey" has no exact match in the closed type list. Peat=none per general American-whiskey category norm.
Sourced small-batch bourbon (6 Year). American bourbon mash bills do not use peated malt, but no source specific to this brand was opened, hence confidence=low.

No producer identified this session (no useful search hits). peatProfile=none rests on the general bourbon-is-unpeated category convention, not a brand-specific source (matches this project's own batch-08 precedent for an equally unconfirmed US bourbon label).

Blairfindy is a real historic place/castle name in the Glenlivet area of Speyside (Wikipedia's Glenlivet article surfaces it), likely used here as an independent single-cask label name rather than a distillery of its own -- region/legalRegion given from that toponymy alone (low confidence). Treated as an undisclosed-origin label per the brief's rule 3: producer and true source distillery not guessed.
Likely named after the Irish folk-song character "Bold Thady Quill"; no producer identified this session.

Wikipedia: the modern 'Bomberger's'-branded whiskey (e.g. 'Bomberger's Declaration' in my sample) is a Michter's product with 'no direct connection' to the historic 1753-1989 Bomberger's/Michter's Distillery site in Pennsylvania (a National Historic Landmark, now non-operating). parentSlug=michters is not a row in my own producer.tsv - Michter's is a well-known US whiskey brand/producer another batch will very likely cover; flag if it does not. peatProfile via the generic bourbon-category fact.

Believed (general knowledge, not confirmed this session) to be a Bladnoch-associated blended Scotch from an earlier ownership era; the current Bladnoch site does not list it and no other citation was found.

Single generic product line with no other qualifier; "Boulevardier" is otherwise a classic bourbon/Campari/vermouth cocktail name, so this may be a bottled RTD cocktail mis-filed under whisky rather than an actual whiskey brand (same concern as Ice Drive, see final report) rather than a whiskey brand -- left fully unknown.
Standard Diageo blended Scotch since 1884; no peat or smoke character mentioned in sourced material.
Undisclosed-distillery label, same pattern as Secret Orkney - likely Highland Park or Scapa, deliberately not guessed per brief rule 3.
American rye whiskey; specific producer not identified this session. Treated at the American-rye category default (unpeated).
No web presence found (single product, no distinguishing sample). Irish-themed own-label blend pattern, category default applied per the brief's long-tail rule.

Moldovan single malt (3-year, "Original Scottish Technology" claim) plus flavoured Honey/Apple variants, so defaultTypeName left empty. No smoke/peat mentioned in the thin, partly foreign-language sourcing available
Not researched (budget). "Crater Lake" is a well-known Oregon, US landmark; countryCode/defaultTypeName inferred from the name, peat left unknown per no-citation policy.
Own-label blended Scotch, no web presence found; fast-tracked per own-label rule.

No country stated by the catalogue and no specific producer identified this session (named for the Kentucky waterfall). peatProfile=none rests on the general bourbon-is-unpeated category convention, not a brand-specific source.
Product name explicitly says 'Tennessee Straight', the basis for countryCode=US/defaultTypeName=tennessee; producer/distillery not identified this session
Single-product own label; could not identify this brand this session (WebSearch budget exhausted). Fast/cheap long-tail treatment per the brief; left fully unknown rather than guessed.
No information found within budget. Single sample name is 'Gold Mill', which does not obviously relate to the brand name 'Dilmoor' - origin and type could not be determined.
No web presence found this session; "Dram"/"Loch" naming strongly suggests an own-label Scotch blend.

Craft distillery, Spokane, Washington -- confirmed real via the American Distilling Institute wiki page (2010/2011 Bubble Cap "Distillery of the Year"). Known for wheat whiskey (not one of the 8 listed defaultTypeName values, left empty). American whiskey categories are not peated.
No dedicated source found; own-label Irish blend inferred from the name. Peat via the Irish-whiskey category source.
